predecessors.name: Kamarupa
predecessors.text: central Assam, south bank (the Kachari kingdom): the kamarupa-kingdom dossier's successor land

successors.name: East India Company
successors.text: the Cachar plains (annexed 1832) and the North Cachar hills (1834), as the east-india-company dossier draws them

ledger.x: 1228: the Kachari kingdom stands between the Dikhu and the Kolong as the Ahoms arrive.
1526: the Ahoms march on the Kachari at Marangi.
1536: the Kachari frontier settles at the Kolong.
1536: the Kolong country passes to the Ahoms.
1558: the Kachari court re-forms at Maibang after 22 years without a king.

c. 1644: the Kachari leave the Dhansiri valley. 'By the reign of Birdarpan Narayan (reign around 1644), the Dimasa rule had withdrawn completely from the Dhansiri valley.' The page does not say who took it.
1745: the Khaspur Koch state merges into the Kachari kingdom.
c. 1750: the seat moves from Maibang to Khaspur. 'The centre of administration was moved from Maibang to Khaspur', which Shin dates to 1745, 1750 or 1755.
1832: the Cachar plains are annexed by the British.
1834: the North Cachar hills are annexed.

wars.name: Ahom-Kachari conflict
wars.outcome: Ahom advance: Marangi taken in 1526, peace on the Dhansiri, Dimapur occupied in 1536 and the Kolong made the Ahom frontier; the Kachari capital Dimapur abandoned.

wars.name: Turbak's invasion of Assam
wars.outcome: The Kachari kingdom supported the Ahoms against the Bengal commander Turbak (1532/1533); no territorial result.

wars.name: Koch conquest of the Kachari kingdom
wars.outcome: After 'subjugating the Ahoms in 1564' Chilarai 'advanced on Marangi' and made the Dimasa kingdom a Koch feudatory; he set up the Koch administration at Brahmapur (Khaspur) in 1562.

wars.name: Ahom-Kachari conflict of 1618
wars.outcome: Jasa Manik's manipulation 'bring the Dimasa Kacharis into conflict with the Ahoms once again in 1618'; no territorial result is on the page.

wars.name: Rudra Singha's invasion of Cachar
wars.outcome: 'The Ahom King Rudra Singha invaded Kachar in December 1706' and 'destroyed its forts in 1706'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Ahom-Dimasa skirmishes
wars.outcome: 'A number of small skirmishes between the Ahoms and the Dimasas from 1803 to 1805'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: British annexation of Cachar
wars.outcome: Annexed under the doctrine of lapse after Govinda Chandra's death in 1830: the plains in 1832, the hills in 1834.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line before the British annexation; the Dhansiri and Kolong rivers are the named boundaries, and every disc is the researcher's or the ahom-kingdom and east-india-company dossiers' reading.
